newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices crumble again on weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices crumble again on weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices crumbled again Friday in quiet trade, still pressured by concerns about eastern stock levels and mostly-seasonal weather forecasts for next week, industry sources said.
With little exteme weather on the horizon, traders said utilities were stepping up the pace of withdrawals to avoid getting caught with too much inventory at the end of winter.

"Everyone's hitting storage pretty good now, and because there's no (cold) weather, prices are crumbling," said one Texas-based trader. Gulf Coast swing prices slumped 10 cents Friday to the mid-$2.30s, now more than 50 cents below index.
Traders said the rising stock surplus in the East, now 153 bcf or 23 percent over last year, was a growing concern, particulary with only six weeks of winter left.

Prices in south Texas again lost ground, with gas on Tetco off more than five cents to the $2.30 area, 45 cents below Feb 1 levels. While no major cold was forecast for Texas next week, traders said prices there would remain vulnerable to cold weather spikes, with producing region stocks still more than 15 percent below year-ago, according to AGA data.
In west Texas, Permian prices were a dime lower in the mid-$2.20s, more than 30 cents below index.
Midcontinent prices tumbled more than a nickel to the low-$2.30s, about 40 cents below Feb 1.
In the East, New York city-gate weekend gas prices slipped about a dime to about $2.90.
Swing prices at the southern California border were pegged more than five cents lower in the low-$2.40s.
